title: Video Released in Controversial Shooting
description:
This video is sponsored by SafetyVid.org which uses a network of 10,000 cameras to automatically capture video of highway crashes. Yes, you can get video of YOUR crash today at SafetyVid.org.
 
Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

MIDWEST SAFETY:
Promoting transparency in government for the safety of the public.

transcript.text: Three years after the shooting of Winston Smith in Minneapolis, Minnesota's Bureau of Criminal Apprehension released the footage, taken by Smith himself. The incident sparked several months of protests with activists claiming Smith was assassinated. U.S. Marshals, who conducted the arrest, do not wear body cameras, so no video was believed to have captured the shooting. Until now. Winston, please let them take you. Like, what the... Open the door, Winston, babe. Please, open the door! Just shoot. Winston, open the door, Winston! Winston, open the door! Just shoot! The Justice Department now requires federal agents to wear body cameras when executing arrest warrants or searching buildings after local police departments ceased aiding the Marshal Service's fugitive task force until federal body cam policies changed. Hennepin and Crow Wing County Attorney's offices decided not to charge the task force members with any crimes.
